580.text: Health equity in cancer outcomes is the absence of disparities for people with different levels of social advantage. 1

590.text: Person-centred care means informing and involving people in their care, and respecting and responding to their individual needs, preferences and values, as well as those of their families and carers. 2

599.text: Safe and quality care means delivering the most appropriate and best-value care, while keeping people safe from preventable harm in the delivery of that care. 3

608.text: Multidisciplinary care is an integrated team approach that involves all relevant health professionals discussing all relevant treatment options and making joint recommendations about treatment and supportive care plans that consider the individual characteristics and preferences of the person with cancer. 4

617.text: Supportive care involves prevention and management of the adverse effects of cancer and its treatment, including management of physical and psychological symptoms and side effects across the cancer continuum. Supportive care aims to improve the quality of rehabilitation, secondary cancer prevention, survivorship, and end-of-life care. 5

626.text: Navigation and care coordination are related person-centred interventions that aim to empower patients, families and carers affected by cancer to facilitate safe and timely access to optimal cancer-related care and support. 6

635.text: Good communication is an essential part of cancer care and a responsibility of everyone involved in health care across the cancer continuum. 7

644.text: Research and clinical trials generate evidence to improve understanding of cancer and to accelerate progress in prevention, detection, diagnosis, treatment, supportive care, survivorship care, palliative and end-of-life care. 8

2728.text: 3.2.3 Pharmacogenetics Pharmacogenetics can influence the effectiveness of treatment and the risk of adverse effects. Applying pharmacogenetic information to treatment planning can help ensure patients receive the most appropriate drug at the optimal dose from the start of treatment. 23

2856.text: Treatment planning should be undertaken by a multidisciplinary team. The multidisciplinary team should meet to discuss newly diagnosed patients and recommend a treatment plan. 2859.text: Multidisciplinary input should be considered for all patients with cancer. Any people whose cases are not discussed at a multidisciplinary team meeting should at minimum be named on the agenda for noting.
